passage: The list went up at 3:55, five minutes before the school bus left. Binita's name wasn't on the debate team. She had practised for three weeks. The student council results went up on the corridor board in Oslo on a grey Tuesday. Priscila's name was third out of three.

Anders found her by the lockers. "Hey. You okay?"

She almost said, "Yeah, fine, whatever." It was on her tongue. Instead she took a breath. "Actually, no. I'm disappointed. And kind of embarrassed. I gave that speech in front of everyone and I got the fewest votes."

Anders nodded slowly. "That makes sense. I'd feel the same."

Saying it out loud made her throat loosen. She could feel her face cooling down. They walked to the canteen, and by the time they'd queued for waffles she was able to joke that at least now she had Tuesday afternoons free.

That evening she watched a clip of her speech. It was better than she'd remembered. She wrote down two things she'd change if she ran again next year.

qa.a: Priscila felt disappointed and embarrassed, since she had given a speech in front of everyone and got the fewest votes.
